newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger sees up to $50-mln Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger sees up to $50-mln Q4 charge.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said on Thursday it would take a pre-tax restructuring charge of up to $50 million in the fiscal fourth quarter.
The charge will cover elimination or rearrangement of certain fixed assets, and an expected reduction of worldwide headcount by up to seven percent, or about 500 employees, the company said.
The charge is related to a restructuring of the company's Beloit Corp unit, the sole North American producer of pulp and paper machinery and systems, it said.
The plans were disclosed to analysts in New York by Harnischfeger officials whose remarks were released here by the company.

"The plan is expected to be fully implemented by the year 2000. Beloit's sales, currently running at just over $1 billion, are targeted to approach $2 billion in 2000 with an operating profit return on sales of 13 to 15 percent upon full implementation," Harnischfeger said.

"Further, the plan is targeted to produce increasingly positive EVA (economic value added) and cash flow beginning in 1997, with targeted improvements in operating profit of $10 million in 1997, $65 million in 1998, $90 million in 1999 and $105 million in 2000," the company said.

The new strategy for Beloit results from an intensive, nine-month study of business operations, trends in paper consumption and distribution, and discussions with customers, suppliers and employees, the company said.
Shares in the papermaking, mining and material handling equipment manufacturer were up 1/2 to 39-5/8.
